newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu calls for "balanced" EU peace efforts.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu calls for "balanced" EU peace efforts.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he would press European leaders during his forthcoming European tour to adopt a more balanced approach to Middle East peace efforts.

"I intend to turn to European leaders and press to establish the need to adopt a more balanced, factual and responsible stance because this will only help move the peace process forward," Netanyahu said.

The Israeli leader was due to leave on Wednesday night on a four-day trip to the Hague and Rome for talks with the Dutch European Union presidency, Italian and Dutch leaders, businessmen and Jewish groups.

Israel has said European moves in the United Nations to censure its decision to build a Jewish settlement in disputed East Jerusalem, claimed by both Israel and the PLO, harmed EU efforts to mediate between it and the Palestinians.
The United States, Israel's key ally, last month twice vetoed U.N. Security Council resolutions condemning the housing plan that has plunged Middle East peace moves into crisis.

"The expectation of the Palestinians and the Arab world that Europe will always stand behind every claim and violation of theirs and ignore facts...is one of the obstacles that prevent us from moving forward in a balanced process," Netanyahu said.

A spokesman for EU special Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos told Reuters Moratinos and the Dutch presidency would on Thursday present Netanyahu with a European initiative to help revive Israeli-PLO peace moves.
"It has been sent to the Americans and it should be presented to Mr Netanyahu tomorrow," the spokesman said.

The peace process began to crumble after Netanyahu broke ground on the East Jerusalem project on March 18, touching off fierce West bank unrest. The crisis deepened when a Palestinian suicide bomber killed three Israelis at a Tel Aviv cafe three days later.

The EU initiative calls on both parties to abstain from unilateral actions, for Israel to agree to a freeze of Jewish settlement in occupied lands and for a reinforced Palestinian commitment to fight "terrorism", the spokesman said.
"The initiative proposes a code of conduct to the Israelis and Palestinians to create an atmosphere of confidence in order to favour the resumption of talks," he said.
But Israel rejects any link between Palestinian moves to halt violence and its settlement activities.
"If there is any connection between stopping building and stopping violence, it is unacceptable for civilised societies," Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters.
